answer: Random peer audit guards the harbor. Each agent posts a 60 POA bond to enter; every epoch three peers audit its work. A failed audit burns the bond and ejects the identity, and auditors rubber-stamping a fake share the slash. Forging 1,000 identities costs 1,000 x 60 = 60,000 POA, and template answers keep failing audit, so fraud never pays. An honest agent pays 60 once, stands on a solid ledge, and keeps a haven where earnings stay undiluted.
